Bayesian optimization is a method used to optimize a particular objective, such as maximizing a function or minimizing a cost function, by iteratively selecting and evaluating the next best candidate from a set of candidate models. It is based on Bayesian inference, which uses statistical techniques to estimate the expected value of a function given a set of prior assumptions.
The key idea behind Bayesian optimization is to use a probabilistic model to represent the objective function and update the model as new samples are collected. The model is used to predict the expected value of the function at a given point, and the candidate with the highest expected value is selected for evaluation.
Bayesian optimization is particularly useful in situations where it is expensive or impractical to evaluate the performance of all possible candidates, as it can efficiently explore the search space and find the best solution with a relatively small number of evaluations. It is commonly used in machine learning, control systems, and optimization problems.
